newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian cattlemen see eventual Argentine threat.
newsitem.headline: Australian cattlemen see eventual Argentine threat.

text.p: Argentina did not pose an immediate threat to Australian beef exports to Asia but was likely to do so in the longer term, The Australian Cattlemen's Union said on Tuesday.
It was commenting on Argentina being officially declared foot-and-mouth disease free with vaccination by the International Epyzootic Office in Paris.

"It is time to take up the challenge and realise that Argentina is expected to be declared foot and mouth disease free towards the end of the decade," research officer Dominic Nolan said in a statement.

Argentina was involved in ongoing negotiations with Japan, South Korea and Indonesia, although these were unlikely to succeed given tight regulations of vaccinated product in these countries, he said.
Richard Koch, economist with the meat industry statutory authority, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp, said the new classification did not allow for direct exports to north Asia.
But it did place Argentina, which has a cattle herd twice the size of Australia's, to be in a good position when disease-free status without vaccination was given, he said.
